text:
jin: Quick thread: building a tiny sample app that runs Redwood JS SDK in Deno Deploy and Bun Edge — hitting module resolution + typing surprises.

lina: what surprises?

jin: Deno refuses to import the package by name: `Import 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@redwood/inference@1.2.0' failed: Not a valid URL`. I tried deno.land/x and skypack but typing breaks.

oliver: For Deno you usually need an explicit ESM bundle URL or an import_map. Two approaches:
1) publish an ESM single-file build to a CDN and import that URL;
2) add an `import_map.json` in the sample with the package name -> CDN URL mapping and instruct `deno run --import-map=import_map.json`.

lina: For Bun Edge we saw `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` when bundlers pick the CJS main. Bun's resolver follows package.exports. If the package.json doesn't include \"types\" under exports it picks CJS.

jin: Any quick fix so the sample app isn't confusing?

oliver: Add an `edge-samples/deno.ts` and `edge-samples/bun.ts` with explicit imports. Example Deno header:
```ts
// deno.ts
import Redwood from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@redwood/inference@1.2.0/dist/esm/index.js";
```
and mention `--allow-net` in the README.

lina: Types: TS in Deno complains because the published `index.d.ts` uses `export =` and our sample tsconfig (Deno supports `tsconfig.json` but ignores `typesVersions`) — simplest short-term is to ship a `deno.d.ts` shim in the sample that re-exports proper ESM types: 
```ts
export { Client } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@redwood/inference@1.2.0/dist/esm/index.d.ts";
```
Not pretty but it stops the red squiggles.

jin: Nice. What about fetch + streaming? Deno's fetch works but the streaming body is a reader that Deno's `Response` exposes differently. My streaming handler crashes in Bun.

oliver: Detection pattern helps: `if (typeof (res.body as any)?.getReader === 'function') { /* use WHATWG reader */ } else { /* handle Node/Bun stream */ }` Also add `TextDecoder` fallback for older Bun versions.

lina: Crypto: we had to replace `createHmac` Node calls. For edge runtimes prefer WebCrypto APIs and avoid node-only `crypto.createHmac`. Provide a small adapter in SDK: `hash(data){ return subtle.digest('SHA-256', data) }` and a tiny util to convert ArrayBuffer->hex.

oliver: Agree. Also add note: \"do not rely on package main field for ESM usage in edge runtimes\" and include examples of `package.json` exports we want — e.g., \"\"exports\": { \".\": { \"import\": \"./dist/esm/index.js\", \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/index.js\" }, \"./package.json\": \"./package.json\" }\". That helps Bun + modern Node.

jin: For onboarding friction: sample repo should include 1) `deno.json` or import_map, 2) `bunfig.toml` note, 3) `tsconfig.json` with `skipLibCheck` comment, 4) small `edge-compat.ts` with helpers.

dev-bot: gist created: https://gist.github.com/dev-team/edge-sdk-samples (private) :white_check_mark:

lina: Could we add automated test in CI that runs the sample with `deno run` and `bun --version` smoke tests? Even a quick `deno cache` + `bun --version` would catch import regressions.

oliver: Yep. I'll add a workflow `samples/edge-smoke.yml` that does `deno cache deno.ts` and `bun --version` inside matrix.

jin: Perfect. I'll push an initial PR with samples + README guidance mentioning explicit ESM imports, import_map usage, lazy-auth pattern for no-timers, and the crypto adapter.

lina: Thanks — much better than repeating "just use node" in onboarding.

dev-bot: PR 482 opened: samples/edge-compat + CI smoke tests.
